trial_court: Family Court, Surajpur, Civil Suit No.30A/2020
case_name: Salendra @ Sumit Soni vs Surendra Kumar Soni

parties.respondent_defendant: Surendra Kumar Soni and Sangeeta Soni, defendants

facts_of_case: The plaintiff filed a civil suit for declaration of son and property rights. The Family Court dismissed the application under Section 34 of Specific Relief Act, 1963.

legal_principles.principle: A suit cannot be dismissed on account of misjoinder of parties.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble Supreme Court in catena of decisions held that the suit cannot be dismissed on account of misjoinder of party and the plaintiff cannot be deprived of justice, as such, it is incumbent upon the Court to get the mistake rectified directing the plaintiff to make the correction.
cited_cases: Union of India Vs. V.R. Tripathi, (2019) 14 SCC 646
Revanasiddappa & Anr. v. Mallikarjun & Ors., (2011) 11 SCC 1
Bharatha Matha & Anr. v. R. Vijaya Renganathan & Ors., (2010) 4 AIR SCW 3503
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to ensure plaintiff's right to justice

legal_principles.principle: A suit is not barred by limitation if it was earlier filed before the regular Civil Court and later referred to the Family Court.
legal_principles.held: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the suit was earlier filed before the regular Civil Court on 25.02.2017 but on account of establishment of Family Court the matter was referred to the Family Court returning the plaint on 03.02.2020 to the plaintiff, as such, it cannot be held that the suit was barred by limitation and there is no fault on the part of the appellant/plaintiff.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to clarify the timeline for suit filing
